newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Taiwan envoy lodges strong protest with South Africa.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan envoy lodges strong protest with South Africa.

text.p: Taiwan's ambassador to South Africa said on Thursday he had lodged a very strong protest with the government of President Nelson Mandela over the "totally unexpected" announcement that Pretoria would downgrade its ties with Taiwan in order to open diplomatic relations with Beijing.
Ambassador I Cheng Loh told a news conference he had been given only 28 hours notice over the move and was very surprised by what he called "really quite unusual diplomatic practice".

Loh said he had been informed on Tuesday by Mandela of South Africa's intention to change its policy, but ..."I thought he had given us 13 months to talk to the South African government" before the decision to recognise the Communist Peoples' Republic became final.
"It is really quite unusual diplomatic practice...I am as surprised as you are about the timeframe because it does not conform to international practice," he said.

Loh said it was too early to say what the impact would be on trade between the two countries. Investment was another matter, he said, and there were "dozens of (joint) projects" which would now have to be reviewed by Taiwan's legislature.

Asked about a comment by South Africa's former president, F.W. de Klerk, that senior communists in Mandela's ruling bloc had influenced the decision, Loh replied: "I must confess I tend to agree with Mr de Klerk."
